# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Decompose the `downtime-worker.ts` god class

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (8,105 lines, 174 exported symbols, 23 logical sections)

## Problem statement

`downtime-worker.ts` has grown into a single 8,105-line module that carries the
entire downtime-dispatch subsystem: constants, public types, idle detection,
the local-status poller, dispatchability gates, the Herdr list-head dispatch
pipeline, leader-election coordination, pane spawning and lifecycle, the worker
tick orchestrator, wl-output parsers, per-tier selection, settings clamps and
round-robin helpers. Navigating, reviewing and safely changing any one concern
requires holding the whole file in view, so every dispatch change carries
avoidable regression risk.

## Users

- **Downtime-dispatch maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one
  concern (e.g. a gate, a tier parser, the spawn path) without reasoning about
  8,000 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need to review a focused diff where the blast radius of
  a change is legible from the touched module.
- **Future agents implementing dispatch work items** need small, named modules
  they can locate with a file search instead of reading a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent implementing a dispatch-gate change, I want the gate logic in a
  dedicated module so that I can modify it without re-reading the whole worker.
- As a reviewer, I want a split diff to be attributable to a single concern so
  that I can verify it against its own tests.
- As a maintainer, I want each module under 1,000 lines so that the file is
  readable in a single pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (now a thin barrel) and for every
   module created by the split.
2. **Public surface preserved — used symbols only.** Every symbol currently
   imported from `./downtime-worker.js` by another module remains exported from
   that exact path with identical types and values, so the 33 importing files
   compile with no import-path edits. The barrel re-exports **only symbols that
   are actually used** by consumers; symbols that nothing outside the split
   modules imports are internal and need not be re-exported (producer decision
   on Q2).
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change;
   no test file is modified (not its import paths, fixtures or assertions), and
   all 15 `downtime-worker.*` test suites plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite
   pass unchanged.
4. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `downtime-worker.js` barrel; the dependency
   check reports no new cycles and does not extend the pre-existing
   `stalled-work ↔ downtime-worker` type-only cycle into runtime values.
5. **Single-flight state remains singular.** The module-level mutable
   `dispatchInFlightCount` (current line 2523) lives in exactly one module and
   is not duplicated by the split, so per-process dispatch single-flight
   semantics are unchanged.
6. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and the existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and update imports; do not refactor logic,
  rename public symbols, or change behaviour.
- **Barrel compatibility.** 33 files import from `./downtime-worker.js`,
  including 15 `downtime-worker.*` test suites (~15,000 test lines) and the
  production consumers `index.ts`, `settings.ts`, `ship-guard.ts`,
  `fetcher.ts`, `stalled-work.ts`, `worklist.ts`, plus 11 other test files.
  The barrel preserves that contract.
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf modules first (constants,
  types, clamps/parsers) and work inwards, so each merged step leaves the build
  and the full suite green.
- **No new runtime dependencies**, no test-file rewrites, no changes to the wl
  CLI contract or dispatch behaviour.
- **Scope boundary.** The item targets `downtime-worker.ts`; the other
  `packages/herdr` files above 1,000 lines are explicitly out of scope (see
  Risks — scope creep).

## Existing state

`downtime-worker.ts` is 8,105 lines. Its section inventory (line ranges from the
current `dev` checkout) is:

| # | Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---------|-------|------|
| 1 | Constants | 204–616 | 413 |

| `downtime-worker.coordination.ts` | `computeMostImportantItem`, `dispatchFromCoordination`, `runCoordinationCheckIn`, leader-election glue | ~1,000–1,300 (likely split into offers/leader) |
| `downtime-worker.orchestrator.ts` | `createDowntimeWorker` tick loop | ~930 |
| `downtime-worker.ts` | Thin barrel re-exporting the full public surface | ~150–250 |

Where a candidate module would still exceed 1,000 lines (coordination, dispatch),
it is split further along an existing section boundary rather than left oversized.

# Intake Brief — Reduce per-invocation cost of the transient `wl` processes (WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B)

## Problem statement (headline)

Every `wl` command spawns a fresh Node.js process that takes **0.6–1.7 s and 80–180 MB** just to boot (a bare `node -e ''` is 0.35 s / 58 MB): the CLI eagerly imports 40+ modules (commander, all ~35 command builders, plugins, runtime, `better-sqlite3`) before any command logic, and herdr panes + pi agents fire these one-shot processes continuously (30 s refresh ticks, 60 s `sync --if-idle` per pane, per-agent polls). Four concurrent `wl` processes were observed at 25–65 % CPU each — bursty, seconds-long, gone moments later. The shipped read-cache (WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3) cut *read work* (83 %) but deliberately left process spawning unchanged ("each invocation still spawns a wl process"). There is also an unbounded hygiene leak: `~/.cache/wl/state/` holds **216,228 one-file-per-worklog-dir counters (~890 MB, 216k inodes)** that are never pruned.

## Users

- **Herdr TUI panes / pi agents** — the heaviest spawners; every 30–60 s tick pays full process boot even for cache hits.
  - *As a herdr pane, I want cache-hit refreshes to cost near bare-node boot, so refresh cycles stop stealing core-seconds from the host.*
- **Operators / agents running ad-hoc `wl` commands** — every `wl create/update/comment/sync/next` pays the same boot cost.
  - *As an operator, I want `wl` commands to feel instant, so interactive and agent-driven use stops producing CPU bursts.*
- **Host administrators** — transient process bursts and an unbounded 890 MB cache dir degrade a shared Raspberry Pi / herdr server.
  - *As an admin, I want spawn load and cache disk bounded, so the host stays responsive.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **(AC1)** **Import budget on the fast path:** the cache-hit read path and `--version` must not load command modules, the DB runtime, or plugins. Measured on the reference host (this repo, node ≥ 20): p95 wall time for a warm repeated `wl next --json` / `list --status open --json` cache hit ≤ **0.5 s** and peak RSS ≤ **60 MB** (current: ~0.6–1.2 s / 80–160 MB; bare node 0.35 s / 58 MB — the margin is deliberately tiny, so the fast-path import set must be slimmer than today's `read-cache-cli` graph at 61 MB). Enforced by a regression benchmark/test (e.g. asserts the heavy modules are not imported on the fast path).
- **(AC2)** **Measurable spawn-load reduction:** total CPU-seconds per 30 s refresh cycle across ≥ 4 panes on one shared worklog dir drops **≥ 60 %** versus current behaviour, measured by extending the env-gated spawn instrumentation (`WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE`, src/spawn-counter.ts) to record per-process CPU time (`process.resourceUsage().user+system`); baseline and after numbers quoted in the work item.
- **(AC3)** **Cache hygiene / bounded on-disk state:** `~/.cache/wl/state/` (216,228 files, ~890 MB, one file per worklog dir ever seen) is bounded and prunable — after a run, state storage is capped (bounded file count, or consolidated storage) and stale entries are removed; a documented maintenance path (`wl doctor cache` or automatic pruning) reclaims it. Freshness semantics unchanged (no correctness regression).
- **(AC4)** **No correctness regression:** all read-cache invariants from WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 hold — write→read freshness, arg-variant separation, WAL-aware invalidation, concurrent readers/writers, byte-identical JSON for identical (dir, argv, version). The existing read-cache/e2e/spawn-reduction suites pass unchanged.
- **(AC5)** **Graceful degradation:** if lazy loading or the split entry point fails for any command, behaviour falls back to today's fully-registered CLI (no functional regression, help/plugin registration intact).
- **(AC6)** **Tests + docs:** unit/integration/benchmark tests cover the fast path, lazy loading, CPU-time instrumentation and cache hygiene; related documentation (CLI.md / CONFIG.md / docs as appropriate) updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Stateless one-shot CLI** — no daemon, no long-lived server, no IPC worker (operator decision, Q1-A). Architecture and on-disk Git/JSONL sync semantics must not change.
- `wl` must keep working from any worktree/`--worklog-dir` (the prefix-to-sibling resolution and worklog-dir override must not be disturbed by splitting the entry point).
- Cache correctness invariants (WAL aware, TTL 30 s, LRU bound) are **non-negotiable** — the fast path only shortens import time.
- Node ESM, build via `tsc` to `dist/`; `/usr/local/bin/wl` symlinks into this repo's `dist/cli.js` (v1.0.22) — keep that contract intact.
- Performance benchmarks must be CPU-time based / tolerant on shared hosts (a Raspberry Pi, herdr server).

## Existing state

- Read-cache epic **shipped (WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3, v1.0.9)**: identical JSON reads (list/next/show/search/status) served pre-parse from `~/.cache/wl` with 83 % read-work reduction, sync+heartbeat, herdr in-process memoisation. Its audit records the accepted variance: "each invocation still spawns a wl process that exits without DB work" — the spawn itself was left in scope.
- pi-extension poll gating shipped (WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N + tests WL-0MSB446N4009FFT5); orphaned worktree process lifecycle shipped (WL-0MRP1SLZB005ZNYO).
- Herdr cadence: 30 s refresh × 4–5 wl fetches per pane, 60 s auto-sync with 45 s cross-instance heartbeat (packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts).
- Measured here: `node -e ''` 0.35 s/58 MB; `wl --version` 0.95 s/80 MB; `wl list --json` (repeated) 0.6–1.2 s/80–160 MB; `wl status` 1.74 s/180 MB; `wl sync --if-idle` 1.39 s/116 MB; importing `dist/cli-utils.js` alone 0.60 s/73 MB; `dist/read-cache-cli.js` 0.46 s/61 MB.

## Desired change

1. **Split the entry point:** keep `src/cli.ts` thin — argv scan + read-cache fast path (imports only `read-cache-cli`, `spawn-counter`, `worklog-paths` + minimal utils), then **dynamically import** the current heavy graph (`./cli-main.ts` or lazy command map). Cache hits and `--version` exit before commander/DB/plugins load.
2. **Lazy per-command imports:** replace the 35 eager `import XCommand` lines with a registry resolving each command on demand; `--help` / bare invocation may load all (rare).
3. **Extend spawn instrumentation** with per-process CPU time (ru_utime/ru_stime) to measure CPU-second reduction, not just spawn count.
4. **Cache hygiene:** bound/prune `~/.cache/wl/state/` (e.g. LRU/TTL over counter files, consolidate counters, housekeeping in `wl doctor`); optionally tidy stale top-level entries.
5. **If ≥60 % CPU-second reduction is not reached by import slimming alone** (spawn count unchanged), coalesce repeated herdr reads into fewer wl invocations (still stateless, e.g. one batch query per refresh tick) — record which lever was needed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/cli.ts` — split entry: 40 eager imports (lines ~6–47), cache fast path (~526–545) that currently runs only after the full graph loads.
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — cache lookup/backfill/invalidation orchestration; the fast-path import set.
- `src/read-cache.ts` — `state/` counter files (`stateCounterFilePath`/`bumpStateCounter`, ~157–200), purge/LRU, entry layout.
- `src/spawn-counter.ts` — extend `SpawnRecord` with CPU time.
- `src/commands/*.ts` — command modules to lazy-load (next, list, status, show, search, sync, …).
- `src/plugin-loader.ts`, `src/cli-utils.ts`, `src/lib/runtime.ts` — heavy imports to defer.
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — cache maintenance command (state pruning).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — coalescing repeated reads per refresh tick (only if needed to hit AC2).
- Tests: `tests/read-cache.test.ts`, `tests/read-cache-cli.test.ts`, `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts`, `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts`, new `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts` / CPU-time benchmark.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSB19J56006E87J (completed, v1.0.7) — "Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM)"** — the predecessor investigation. It attacked spawn *count* (pi browse-widget idle-gating → WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N, herdr cadence, read-cache). **Not a duplicate:** it left per-invocation *cost* and on-disk cache hygiene untouched; this item targets boot cost + `state/` growth.
- WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 (completed) — read-cache epic; the spawn cost was its accepted variance; this item continues from there.
- WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N / WL-0MSB446N4009FFT5 (completed) — visibility-gated polling in pi extension / herdr (spawn-count side).
- WL-0MRP1SLZB005ZNYO (completed) — orphaned node process lifecycle in worktrees.
- WL-0MRTSPLAX005Y8QY (completed) — process lifecycle documentation (reference for docs conventions).
- WL-0MULOZ37S007VV13 (completed) — metrics collection module (host metric collection precedent; candidate to reuse for CPU-second reporting).
- WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K (completed) — `wl sync` before refactor/standup skills (lock-aware `sync --if-idle` spawners).
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping open/in-progress item targeting wl startup cost; `WL-0MSB19J56006E87J` covers the already-shipped spawn-count remediation only.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Lazy/help registration risk:** commander help and plugin registration must not regress — mitigated by AC5 fallback and deferring full registration to the heavy path.
- **Entry-point tests:** several suites import `src/cli.ts` / `dist/cli.js` directly; splitting must keep those contracts (tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts, inproc-harness, smoke, completion, …).
- **Benchmark flakiness** on shared hosts — AC1/AC2 measured by CPU time, p95 over repeated runs, generous margins above bare-node baseline.
- **State-dir pruning races:** pruning counters concurrently with writers must stay atomic (temp+rename, no regression of counter monotonicity).
- **Scope-creep guard:** daemon/server mode, JSONL/Git sync changes, and TUI redesign are explicitly out of scope — recorded as related opportunities, not work here.
- **Assumption:** the reference-host measurements above are representative of the failing hosts (same repo/worklog versions; herdr panes are the dominant spawner).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — "What's the target shape of the improvement?" — Answer (rgardler): **A — keep `wl` a stateless one-shot CLI; lazy per-command imports, fast path for cache hits/`--version` at near-node-boot cost, plus cache hygiene (prune `state/`, bound growth). No daemon.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 — "How should we measure success?" — Answer (rgardler): **A — total CPU-seconds per refresh cycle ≥ 60 % reduction; per-process RSS < 60 MB; no correctness regression.** Source: interactive reply.
- Research summary: measured per-invocation cost (0.6–1.7 s / 80–180 MB vs 0.35 s / 58 MB bare node), attributed to eager 40-module import graph; verified the read-cache fast path still loads the full graph before serving (src/cli.ts); confirmed unbounded `~/.cache/wl/state/` (216,228 files / ~890 MB) with no pruning path.

## Related work (automated report)

Collected by `/skill:find-related` (sidecar: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B.md`).

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRTSPLAX005Y8QY** — Documentation for process lifecycle management (completed)
- **WL-0MULOZ37S007VV13** — Metrics collection module (completed)
- **WL-0MSB19J56006E87J** — Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — herdr cadence/spawner documentation
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher/claim spawn context
- `CHANGELOG.md` — historical process-spawn/read-cache entries


---

## Plan — feature decomposition (plan skill, 2026-10-19)

Phasing is vertical slices (tracer bullets): measurement first, then the entry-point fast path, then cache hygiene, then the CPU-second verdict and docs. Each slice covers its own code, tests and docs; between phases, review the next items' descriptions and re-check the measured numbers.

| # | Child | Title | Type | Est. | Depends on | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | WL-0MVFRR98A008MM19 | Spawn instrumentation: per-process CPU and RSS | feature | S | — | Measure CPU-time and RSS per spawn (AC1 RSS, AC2) |
| F2 | WL-0MVFRRAXD001E7AN | Startup import-budget harness and baseline | feature | S | F1 | Ratchet + benchmark that lock in AC1 and capture the baseline |
| F3 | WL-0MVFRRCP7007UWS7 | Tests: thin entry-point split and dispatch parity | task | S | F2 | Test-first contracts for the entry split |
| F4 | WL-0MVFRRKKN00544PQ | Split CLI entry: thin fast path, dynamic heavy graph | feature | M | F3 | Fast path exits before commander/DB/plugins load (AC1) |
| F5 | WL-0MVFRREMZ0085G7I | Tests: lazy command registry, help and plugin fidelity | task | S | F4 | Test-first contracts incl. AC5 fallback |
| F6 | WL-0MVFRRMX3003UPP3 | Lazy per-command imports via command registry | feature | M | F5 | Load only the command that runs (AC1, AC5) |
| F7 | WL-0MVFRROLM002K98B | Fast-path import slimming to the 0.5 s / 60 MB budget | feature | M | F2, F4, F6 | Meet and freeze the AC1 numbers |
| F8 | WL-0MVFRRGGC001IQK1 | Tests: cache state pruning, bounds and atomicity | task | S | — | Test-first contracts for AC3 hygiene + AC4 freshness |
| F9 | WL-0MVFRRQ9W003KEFL | Bound and prune cache state via wl doctor cache | feature | M | F8 | Bounded `state/` store + documented maintenance path (AC3) |
| F10 | WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J | Verify >=60% CPU-second reduction per refresh cycle | feature | M | F1, F6, F7 | AC2 measurement and herdr-coalescing verdict |
| F11 | WL-0MVFRRTY5001KTNH | Docs: fast path, instrumentation and cache maintenance | docs | XS | F1, F7, F9 | AC6 documentation half |

### Plan-stage decisions (recorded assumptions)

- **D1 — Budget enforcement is a ratchet, not a single hard-coded threshold.** AC1's 0.5 s / 60 MB budget is tighter than today's fast-path graph (0.46 s / 61 MB), so F2 checks in a budget file (`bench/startup-import-budget.json`) that records the statically reachable graph and the measured cost, and fails on growth. F4 and F7 tighten it in the change that improves it — keeping the suite green between items while locking in every improvement and making the regression test deterministic and host-load tolerant.
- **D2 — Peak RSS comes from the instrumented child.** `process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` is recorded per process by F1, so AC1's RSS check needs no external sampler.
- **D3 — Cache hygiene uses a bounded LRU plus TTL over `state/*.json`.** Consolidating counters into the cache entry files is only adopted if the bounded-file approach misses AC3's cap, because the counter atomicity and monotonicity invariant (`bumpStateCounter`) is the freshness guarantee and must not be rebuilt.
- **D4 — Herdr coalescing is conditional, not assumed.** Desired change #5 is gated behind F10's measurement because herdr already dedupes concurrent identical reads (in-flight memo, WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG) and serves default-view reads in-process via `@worklog/shared` (WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B). The expected remaining gap is per-spawn boot cost.
- **D5 — `--version` uses the generated `src/version.ts`.** `getVersion()` currently lives in the 73 MB `cli-utils` graph; the fast path reads `WORKLOG_VERSION` directly so `wl --version` can exit at bare-node cost.
- **D6 — No daemon, no sync/JSONL changes** (intake Q1-A): the fast path changes only *when* modules load, never what is cached or how sync works.

### Appendix: planning-stage questions and decisions

Intake already recorded Q1 (stateless one-shot CLI, lazy imports, cache hygiene) and Q2 (CPU-second measurement, under 60 MB RSS, no correctness regression). The plan stage asked no new questions: the intake brief's measurements, desired-change list and answered decisions left no ambiguous choice that would change the decomposition. D1–D6 are recorded as assumptions for audit rather than as invented requirements.

- **OPEN QUESTION (for producer, non-blocking):** if F7 cannot reach 60 MB peak RSS (bare node is already 58 MB), should AC1's RSS limit become "within 3 MB of bare node", or should the fast path be allowed further Node startup work (e.g. a compile cache or snapshot)? F7 raises this with measured evidence rather than silently relaxing the AC.

- 2026-10-19 — plan skill: decomposed into 11 child items (F1–F11) in test-first dependency order; created all children at `stage=intake_complete`; wired 15 dependency edges; recorded decisions D1–D6; effort/risk re-estimated from the child WBS.

# Refactor: decompose `packages/shared/src/database.ts` god class

## Problem statement

`packages/shared/src/database.ts` is 3,684 lines and holds a single
`WorklogDatabase` class with 109 methods spanning at least ten unrelated
concerns (work-item CRUD, hierarchy traversal, dependency-edge reconciliation,
comment storage, audit results, FTS/semantic search, sort-index management, the
`wl next` selection pipeline, JSONL import/export, and Git/JSONL sync). It
breaches the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 and is hard to navigate, review, and change safely.

## Users

- **Agents implementing work items** — need to locate the code for one concern
  without reading 3,684 lines; large files inflate context cost and increase
  the chance of editing the wrong overload.
- **Reviewers / producers auditing changes** — need diffs scoped to one
  responsibility; a 3,684-line file makes review of a 20-line behavioural
  change impractical.
- **Operators debugging `wl next`** — need the selection pipeline (the largest
  cluster: ~1,150 lines) to be readable in isolation.

Example user stories:

- As an agent, I want `wl next` selection logic in its own module, so that a
  change to selection ordering does not require loading CRUD, sync and comment
  code into context.
- As a reviewer, I want each extracted module to have a single stated
  responsibility, so that I can judge a diff against one boundary.
- As a maintainer, I want the public `WorklogDatabase` API unchanged, so that
  no CLI/Herdr/TUI consumer needs touching.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ceiling met.** `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and every file under
   `packages/shared/src/database/` is ≤ 1,000 lines (target: largest extracted
   module ≤ 700). Verified with `wc -l` output recorded in the work item.
2. **Public API unchanged.** `WorklogDatabase` (all public method signatures and
   constructor), plus `WorklogDatabaseServices`, `JsonlImportResult`,
   `GitTarget`, `UpdateIfMatchesResult` and `normalizeTitleForMatch` remain
   importable from the unchanged specifier `@worklog/shared` (entry
   `dist/database.js`). No changes to `src/**` or `packages/herdr/src/**`
   consumer code.
3. **Move-only, behaviour-preserving.** No logic, SQL, error-message, ordering,
   or schema changes; existing test assertions are unmodified and the suite is
   green. Test files may be split/moved only where a test file itself exceeds
   1,000 lines (lockstep rule), with import paths the only mechanical change.
4. **No circular imports.** The extracted-module import graph is acyclic; no
   module imports the `database.ts` façade. Shared types live in a context
   module that every extracted module may import.
5. **Responsibilities documented.** `packages/shared/README.md` (Package
   Structure) and each new module's header comment state its single
   responsibility and its boundary.
6. **No performance regression** in the `wl next` path: `npm run
   benchmark:wl-next:json` pre/post comparison within run-to-run noise (the
   extraction moves code only, and `EdgeCache`/effective-priority caching
   semantics are unchanged).
7. **Builds and tests.** `npm run build:shared`, `npm run build` and the full
   project test suite all pass.
8. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes,
   including code comments, `packages/shared/README.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`,
   `docs/dev/fts.md`, `docs/dependency-reconciliation.md` and
   `docs/design/incremental-sync.md` (each currently names
   `packages/shared/src/database.ts` as the home of a concern).

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Extraction and method relocation only; no "while we're here"
  rewrites. Method-level decomposition of the two oversized methods
  (`handleCriticalEscalation`, 324 lines; `findNextWorkItemFromItems`, 251
  lines) is allowed **only** where required to keep an extracted file under the
  ceiling, and must land as a separate commit from the pure move.
- **No public-API growth.** Private hooks needed by extracted modules are
  expressed through an internal context type, not by making `WorklogDatabase`
  members public.
- **Icons import guard (WL-0MT2GMTAZ003VKVL).** `tests/unit/icons.test.ts`
  scans every `.ts`/`.js` file with `ICONS_FILE_RE` and fails on any relative
  `icons.js`/`icons.ts` import. Extracted modules must keep using
  `@worklog/shared/icons`.
- **`src/database.ts` (93-line CLI shim) is unchanged.**
- **No new runtime dependencies.**
- **Serialize with WL-0MVGKGJXJ000ISBU** (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`,
  2,225 lines) — same package and build; running both decompositions
  concurrently would churn `packages/shared/dist` and invite merge conflicts.
- **Escaped backticks** only in written content; Markdown otherwise.

## Existing state

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — 3,684 lines, 6 exports: the
  `WorklogDatabase` class (109 methods), `normalizeTitleForMatch`, and four
  interfaces (`JsonlImportResult`, `GitTarget`, `UpdateIfMatchesResult`,
  `WorklogDatabaseServices`).
- Entry point: `packages/shared/package.json` → `main`/`exports["."]` =
  `./dist/database.js`; `src/database.ts` (root, 93 lines) is a thin CLI
  shim wiring CLI-specific services and re-exporting the shared class.
- Consumers: ~54 files reference the class (`src/**`, `packages/herdr/src/**`,
  `tests/**`, `scripts/**`, `bench/**`), all via `@worklog/shared` or the
  shim — none import internal members.
- Tests in lockstep: `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` (834),
  `database-dedup.test.ts` (134), `dirty-tracking.test.ts` (384),
  `audit-fingerprint-repair.test.ts` (135) — all under 1,000; plus root
  `tests/database.test.ts` (3,651) and `tests/next-regression.test.ts`
  (2,112), which exceed the ceiling and are therefore in scope for
  lockstep splitting.
- **Prior attempt did not land.** WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO ("Decompose
  WorklogDatabase god class", completed) extracted `src/lib/edge-cache.ts` and
  `src/lib/audit-store.ts` on the feature branch only — neither file exists in
  the current tree, and the class has since grown from 2,584 to 3,684 lines.
  This item therefore restarts from a single-class module, and the regrowth is
  the reason the decomposition needs a clear ownership boundary rather than
  ad-hoc extraction.

## Desired change

Extract cohesive modules under `packages/shared/src/database/`, leaving
`database.ts` as a façade that constructs the collaborators and delegates.
Proposed map (method attribution is exhaustive; every current method belongs to
exactly one row):

| Module | Responsibility | Est. lines |
|---|---|---|
| `database.ts` (façade) | Construction/service wiring, delegation, `close()`, existing barrel re-exports | ~400 |
| `database/context.ts` | Shared internal types (`EdgeCache`, database context/hooks), `buildChildrenByParent`, `laterTimestamp`, id generation and prefix accessors, `normalizeTitleForMatch` | ~290 |
| `database/work-items.ts` | Item CRUD (`create`, `createWithNextSortIndex`, `get`, `update`, `updateIfMatches`, `delete`, `list`, duplicate detection, diff helpers) | ~470 |
| `database/hierarchy.ts` | Children/descendants/depth/leaf queries, `cascadePriorityDowngrade`, `demoteParentOnChildAdded`, `revertToPlanComplete` | ~200 |
| `database/dependencies.ts` | Edge CRUD, `buildEdgeCache`, blocker queries, dependency-status reconciliation | ~260 |
| `database/comments.ts` | Comment CRUD, `upsertComments`/`importComments`, activity stamping | ~180 |

| `database/sort.ts` | `sortItemsByScore`, sort-index compute/assign/preview, `reSort`, `orderBySortIndex`, audit-tier comparison, `selectBySortIndex` | ~310 |

  cluster; 324- and 251-line methods). *Mitigation:* pure move first; split
  oversized methods in separate commits; `tests/next-regression.test.ts`
  and `docs/validation/status-stage-inventory.md` act as the behaviour oracle.
- **Circular imports** (`next-pipeline` ↔ `dependencies` ↔ `priority`).
  *Mitigation:* `context.ts` owns shared types; modules receive collaborators
  through the context; façade is never imported by a module.
- **Hidden `this.` coupling.** Several "private" helpers are shared across
  concerns (`buildEdgeCache`, `generateId`, `buildAuditMapForItems`,
  `compareTrackedFields`, `getPriorityValue`, `getNonClosedChildren`,
  `debug`). *Mitigation:* inventory every `this.` call per method before the
  move and express it on the context type.

  `dist/database.js`; the façade must keep that path and re-export every type.

  `npm run benchmark:wl-next:json` before and after the `wl next` cluster.

  single-responsibility headers. A repo-wide file-size guard is **out of
  scope** here and filed separately (see Related work) to avoid scope creep.

  test files only when they are touched in lockstep with their module.

  `scripts/` and `bench/`.

  observed en route becomes a separate `discovered-from` work item.

  (`findNextWorkItemFromItems`).

  `discovered-from:WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT`).

## Appendix: decision log (agent-proposed; producer may override)

No producer interview questions were required: the seed context (goal, drafted
ACs, parent directive) is sufficient to draft an actionable brief, and every
remaining choice is a reversible design decision that the plan/implement stages
can adjust. The three decisions below were taken by the agent and are recorded
for review.

- **Q: How should extracted modules relate to `WorklogDatabase`?**
  **Recommended and chosen: (a)** pure functional modules operating on an
  injected internal context type, with `WorklogDatabase` as a delegating
  façade. Rationale: testable without a database, no inheritance/mixin
  complexity, and the import graph stays acyclic (the façade depends on the
  modules, never the reverse).

  the façade (more state plumbing, harder to test in isolation); (c) mixins /
  `extends` chains (fragile, obscures the public surface).

- **Q: What child granularity?**

  ordering & audit; items & hierarchy; dependencies & comments; search, sync &
  import/export + closeout). Rationale: each child is independently move-only,
  verifiable with the full suite, and small enough to review; the riskiest
  cluster (`wl next`) is isolated so a regression is bisectable.
  Alternatives considered: ~13 children (one per module — more overhead and
  churn than value); one child (no bisectable checkpoints).

- **Q: Add a file-size regression guard (CI/lint) in this item?**
  **Recommended and chosen: no — out of scope.** A guard is repo-wide policy
  affecting every sibling god-class item, not a property of this file.
  Filed as a separate low-priority `chore` item (`discovered-from` this item).

- **Q: Should the oversized test files (`tests/database.test.ts` 3,651;
  `tests/next-regression.test.ts` 2,112) be split?**

# Remove dead top-level `singleFork` key in vitest.config.ts

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

`vitest.config.ts` sets `singleFork: true` at the top level of the `test`
block. Vitest 4 has no such top-level option — `singleFork` is a
`poolOptions.forks.*` key — so the setting is silently ignored (no warning is
emitted). The comment directly above it, "Force per-file isolation by limiting
to 1 active worker per file sequence", describes behaviour that is actually
provided by `isolate: true` + `maxWorkers: 4` (+ `pool: 'forks'`).

The dead key is harmless today, but it is misleading: a future reader may
believe the suite is serialised, and a migration to an option shape that *is*
read (or vitest version churn that starts warning) could confuse diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `singleFork: true` is removed from `vitest.config.ts`.
- The comment above it is rewritten (or removed) to state what actually
  enforces per-file isolation (`pool: 'forks'`, `isolate: true`,
  `maxWorkers: 4`), and that parallelism is otherwise intentional.
- Full canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) stays green with the same
  test counts; no runtime regression in either wall-clock or aggregate test
  time on the same host.

## Out of scope

Bumping `maxWorkers` / `fileParallelism` — that is the follow-up "Test-suite
parallelism: reconsider maxWorkers on hosts with more cores".

# Investigate in-process CLI harness cost (~200 ms per invocation)

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

Timing the in-process CLI harness (`tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts`,
`runInProcess()`, used by `execAsync` in `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts`):

- `--help` (no DB work): ~72 ms per invocation
- `list --json`, `create`, `status`: ~196–257 ms per invocation

The canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) makes roughly 1200 such
in-process invocations — about 240 s of aggregate test time across
`close-recursive` (46 tests), `issue-management` (49), `issue-status` (43),
`valid-json-output` (38) and `json-output-shape` (18), plus seeding in
`beforeEach` hooks.

Every invocation constructs a fresh `Command`, re-registers ~35 built-in
commands, loads config, opens a SQLite database (with schema/migrations) and
closes it. The suite measured 624 s → 427–547 s after WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8, and
this in-process pool is the next largest remaining aggregate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Profile one `runInProcess` call and attribute the per-call cost
  (commander registration vs config load vs DB open/close vs command action).
- Where the cost is test-harness overhead (not production behaviour being
  asserted), reduce it without changing what each test asserts — candidates:
  reusing the command/plugin-context across calls for stateless reads,
  avoiding repeated YAML config parses, sharing DB open across calls within a
  test file.
- If the cost is production CLI startup (DB schema/migrations, plugin scan),
  record the findings and re-scope: the change then belongs in `src/` and is a
  production decision, not a test-only change.
- Canonical suite stays green with unchanged test counts; median wall-clock
  on a consistent host improves versus the pre-change baseline of this item.
data.title: Investigate in-process CLI harness cost (~200 ms/invocation, ~240 s aggregate in canonical suite)

# Test-suite parallelism: reconsider maxWorkers on hosts with more cores

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

The canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) runs with `maxWorkers: 4`
in `vitest.config.ts` (pool `'forks'`, `isolate: true`). The dev host has 16
cores. WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 reduced per-spawn cost ~5× (bundle-based CLI
spawning) and cut the wall clock 30–35 % at matched load, but wall clock
remains dominated by the longest single files on the critical path
(`sync-vs-mutation` ~151 s, `close-recursive` ~121 s, `issue-management`
~88 s, `read-cache-spawn-reduction` ~84 s).

The brief explicitly listed parallelisation as out of scope ("record as
linked follow-up work items, not this brief") — hence this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Measure the canonical suite at `maxWorkers` 4 vs 6 vs 8 on a 16-core host
  (median of ≥3 runs per setting, load quoted per run; report aggregate test
  time as the load-independent metric).
- Confirm memory headroom: RSS per worker tracked; no OOM at the chosen
  setting (the config comment cites memory guardrails as the reason for 4).
- Confirm determinism: 3 consecutive green runs at the chosen setting, no
  intermittent test-timeout or hook-timeout failures.
- Decide and record: either adopt a higher `maxWorkers` (documented) or
  formally keep 4 with the measurement evidence.

## Goal

As a Herdr plugin maintainer, I want the default-view refresh to issue **one** `wl` read per tick — `wl worklist --json` — with the critical, review-queue, in-progress-root and blocked-root guarantees preserved and a fail-open fallback to today's per-subset spawn path when the consolidated read is unavailable.

## Scope

Parent AC2 (single read), AC5 (output parity), AC6 (fetcher tests).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `fetchNextItems(count)` for a default-view refresh issues exactly **one** `runWl` invocation (`worklist`) when the command is available; no `wl list` or `wl next` spawns are issued for the bundle path (the in-flight fetch memo is bypassed for the bundle, or dedupes it, with no extra spawns).
- The mandatory subsets are derived from the bundle: all critical, all in_review (completed + in-progress), all in-progress roots and all blocked roots appear in the returned list regardless of the browse count (existing mandatory-guarantee tests still pass).
- `fetchReviewQueueState()` is derived from the bundle's `reviewQueue` subset (completed-only count + `auditsOutstanding`) and returns the same value as today's standalone `wl list` query for the same DB state.
- Audit enrichment is preserved: for items shared with mandatory `wl list` subsets, the richer `wl list`-style audit fields (`auditResult`, `auditedAt`, `fingerprint`, `currentFingerprint`) win over the `browse` representation, exactly as today (WL-0MUWDW0N6003KF6G).
- Output parity: for the same DB state, the bundle path's final `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems` output is identical to today's per-subset path (test compares both pipelines on the seeded fixture).
- Fail-open: when `wl worklist` is unavailable (older `wl`, non-zero exit, malformed/unparseable payload, missing subset key), the fetcher falls back to the existing per-subset spawns with byte-identical behaviour — the fallback path is asserted by a test that mocks the bundle failure.
- `wl next`'s auto re-sort is NOT triggered by the bundle (pure read); no write byproduct, so the result is deterministically cacheable.
- `--worklog-dir` and managed-worktree resolution behave unchanged (existing worktree tests still pass).
- New tests cover: single-spawn assertion, mandatory-subset presence, review-queue derivation, output parity, and fail-open fallback.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC2: `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` issues that single read per default-view refresh tick; the mandatory-subset guarantees (critical always shown, blocked always shown, review queue always shown) are preserved by tests.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC5: Herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state (existing fetcher tests + the spawn-reduction simulation pass).
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC6: new tests cover the fetcher's single-spawn path, mandatory-subset guarantees and output parity with the per-subset path.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `worklist` to the fetcher's `MEMOIZABLE_COMMANDS` set (bundle is a cacheable read; memo dedupes identical concurrent refreshes — same as today).
2. Add `fetchWorklistBundle()` that runs `runWl(['worklist', '-n', String(count)])`, extracts the five subsets with `extractItems`, and validates the shape (unknown-shape ⇒ fail-open).
3. Rework `fetchNextItems(count)` to: try the bundle → derive mandatory sets + review-queue state + browse feed → merge/enrich with the existing `WL-0MUWDW0N6003KF6G` logic → `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems`; on any failure, fall back to today's `Promise.all([runWl(next), fetchMandatorySubsets()])` exactly.
4. Rework `fetchReviewQueueState()` to read the bundle's `reviewQueue` subset when already fetched in the same refresh, falling back to the standalone query.
5. Add `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` with injected fake `execFileAsync` covering the criteria.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchWorklistBundle`, reworked `fetchNextItems`, `fetchReviewQueueState`, memo set
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` — **new** bundle tests
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-review-queue.test.ts`, `fetcher-include-blocked.test.ts`, `fetcher-inprocess.test.ts` — existing guarantees must keep passing
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` — seeded fixture (from WL-C1)

## Dependencies

- Depends on WL-C2 (`wl worklist` command + payload contract) and WL-C3 (cacheability).
- Depends on WL-C1 only transitively via WL-C2 (fixtures land in WL-C1; tests here reuse them).

## Deliverables

- Single-spawn default-view refresh with preserved mandatory guarantees.
- Review-queue state derived from the bundle.
- Fail-open fallback path.
- Fetcher test coverage including output parity.

## Notes

- Keep the browse feed bounded by the caller's count; mandatory subsets stay unfiltered by count.
- The re-sort write-byproduct risk (parent risk, medium) is handled by the command's `--no-re-sort`-style selection (WL-C2) plus this slice's output-parity test; if parity genuinely differs, record it as a comment and resolve separately rather than making the bundle a write.

As a Herdr pane operator, I want `doRefresh` to run the whole default-view refresh from the single consolidated read — items, review-queue banner state and actionable context — so a refresh tick costs one `wl` process instead of five per pane.

## Scope

Parent AC2 (wire-through), AC5 (unchanged output), AC6 (worklist-level tests).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A default-view `doRefresh` cycle issues exactly **one** `wl` spawn for worklist data (asserted by a spawn-count integration test with an injected exec seam), down from five.

- Filtered views are unchanged: the stage-filtered (`fetchItemsByStage`), priority-filtered (`fetchItemsByPriority`) and recent-dispatches paths still use their existing reads, and the `activeDispatchFilter` path still merges live items from the default fetcher.
- Expanded-parent children still render correctly across the swap (no collapse flicker): the batched in-process children read continues to run concurrently with the consolidated item read, and the existing expand-across-refresh test passes.
- Idle behaviour is preserved: a refresh with no change still spawns zero `wl` processes where it did before (no new unconditional read).
- Event-loop responsiveness: the ≤ 100 ms p95 input-lag guard test still passes.
- Fail-open at the TUI layer: when the consolidated read fails, the refresh shows the per-subset fallback result (or the previous list) instead of an empty or errored view.

1. In `doRefresh`, replace the `fetchReviewQueueState()` + `fetchItemsForView(...)` default-path pair with one consolidated fetch that yields both the items and the review-queue state (e.g. `fetchWorklistBundle()` returns `{ items, reviewState, actionableCount? }`).

- Default-view refresh driven by one consolidated read.

- "One spawn" means one **worklist-data** spawn per tick. The in-process SQLite reads (children, actionable count) are already zero-spawn and stay that way.

# Maintenance routines skill: create/maintain daily scheduled test, standup, refactor sessions at high priority

## Headline

A new ContextHub skill (`/skill:maintenance-routines`) that creates and maintains the required daily scheduled maintenance sessions (test 07:00, standup 08:00, refactor 09:00) in each project's `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatching all of them at **high request priority** so they are processed even in peak periods — backed by a herdr enhancement that threads a per-entry `priority` (default `high`) into the `X-Priority` request header.

## Problem statement

Every project should run regular automated maintenance routines (test suite, standup report, refactor pass). The herdr plugin already has the mechanism (`scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatched on idle by the downtime worker), but there is no maintained, canonical set: the current template/live config only carries `/skill:refactor` (3-day interval, no time) and `/skill:standup` (06:05, no priority), and **no** `/skill:test` routine. Worse, dispatched scheduled prompts have no work item, so they receive the downtime request-priority default `medium` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority(undefined)` → `medium`) — they can be starved behind peak-period contention. The operator wants the three routines scheduled daily (07:00/08:00/09:00) and dispatched at **high** priority.

## Users

- **Project operator** — wants the three routines to reliably exist in each project's schedule and to be processed even in peak periods.
- **Automated maintenance sessions** (`/skill:test`, `/skill:standup`, `/skill:refactor`) — must carry `X-Priority: high` on every provider request so `llama-proxy` serves them ahead of the contention queue.

### Example user stories

- As an operator, I run `/skill:maintenance-routines` on a project and it ensures `/skill:test` (daily 07:00), `/skill:standup` (daily 08:00) and `/skill:refactor` (daily 09:00) are present and correctly configured in `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, without touching my last-run timestamps or any custom entries.
- As an operator, I know every scheduled maintenance session is dispatched with `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY=high` (→ `X-Priority: high`), so the daily test/standup/refactor runs are served even during peak periods.
- As an operator, when I provision a new project with `wl init`, it comes pre-loaded with the same three routines (daily, timed, high priority).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Skill exists and reconciles the schedule.** `skill/maintenance-routines/` ships a `SKILL.md`, a reconciler script and unit tests. Invoking it (or the script directly) reconciles the project-local `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (under the resolved worklog dir) so these required routines are present and exact:
   - `/skill:test` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "07:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:standup` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "08:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:refactor` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "09:00"`, `priority: "high"`
2. **Reconcile is non-destructive and idempotent.** Entries are created if absent; drifted fields (interval/time/priority) are corrected; `lastTriggeredAt` and all other user-defined entries are preserved verbatim; a second run makes no further changes; missing or malformed config files are handled fail-closed with a clear report; `--dry-run` shows the planned diff without writing.
3. **Herdr honours a per-entry `priority` field.** `ScheduledPrompt` gains an optional `priority` (`low|medium|high|critical`) validated in `parseScheduledPrompt` (invalid value → entry skipped with a warning, fail-closed); **absent → defaults to `high`** for scheduled prompts. The scheduled-prompt dispatch passes it through `spawnAgentPane({ priority })` → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` (so `high` → `X-Priority: high` on every request). Unit tests cover parse defaults/validation and the dispatch threading.
